limitations: Original trap entry, C trap handler, core/PLIC dispatch, PLIC API, IRQ init/deinit, timer, exception/syscall/yield and first-task/scheduler-start bodies execute in an emulator over authored memory, CSRs, registers and PLIC claim values; no hardware interrupt is delivered.

xTaskIncrementTick, vTaskSwitchContext, vPortSetupTimerInterrupt, configASSERT, memcpy, memset, device interrupt handlers and non-syscall exception handlers are supplied. Default-handler, null-vector and assert stops are harness stops before an infinite loop, a jump to address zero or an assertion body; mret is not executed.

Andes CSR 0x7c6/0x7c7 names, PLIC register roles and timer units are working interpretations of observed accesses. Interrupt preemption, priority/threshold arbitration, nesting timing, live scheduling and physical timer frequency remain unproved.
